look_here_first: Start below a mature flower head: measure the long, narrow OUTER involucral bracts (calyculus; usually 6–9 mm), then the inner phyllaries (about 7–9+ mm). Check the mostly simple or few-lobed lower leaves and long bare head stalk (peduncle; often 6–15+ cm). Dark red at the ray bases is NOT enough: plains coreopsis (C. tinctoria) can share that color.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Lower leaves deeply divided into narrow segments; upper leaves opposite to alternate and less dissected.

key_traits.label: Heads
key_traits.text: Rays yellow, commonly with dark reddish-brown blotches near the base; disks dark yellow to brownish.

key_traits.label: Phyllaries
key_traits.text: Outer involucre of narrow bracts beneath broader inner phyllaries.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Cypselae flattened, typically with 2 short awns and small marginal teeth/scales.

key_traits.label: Best field traits
key_traits.text: Longer outer calyculus bractlets beneath a mature head (usually 6–9 mm in FNA; photograph side/underside with scale).; Longer inner phyllaries (usually 7–9+ mm) and relatively long head stalks (6–15+ cm).; Basal/cauline leaves simple or 1–2-pinnately lobed with relatively broad terminal lobes; assess several leaves, not a single unusual one.; Yellow rays often with a reddish-brown basal spot or band, supportive only and shared with C. tinctoria.

key_traits.label: Comparison training
key_traits.text: Against Coreopsis tinctoria: compare OUTER head bractlets first (C. basalis usually 6–9 mm; C. tinctoria 1–3+ mm), inner phyllaries (7–9+ versus 4–7[–9] mm), and head stalks (6–15+ versus usually 1–5 cm). C. tinctoria usually has more finely divided stem leaves with narrow threadlike lobes. Flower color alone overlaps. Central Texas narrow-leaved C. basalis can resemble historical C. wrightii concepts; do not force a separate name without taxonomy review.
